<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard AUR PKGBUILD for the SimpleLogin self-hosted email alias server. All source URLs point to the package's declared upstream on GitHub (simple-login/app and simple-login/sl-pgp-rs), which is expected behavior. The prepare() function applies compatibility patches from the local source array, build() runs `npm install` with `--ignore-scripts` (a security-conscious flag that prevents npm lifecycle scripts from executing), and package() performs standard installation into $pkgdir including systemd service units, sysusers, and tmpfiles configuration.

SHA256 checksums are provided for all sources (not SKIP), which is good practice. There is no obfuscated code, no use of eval/base64/curl|bash/wget in suspicious contexts, no data exfiltration, and no backdoors or reverse shells. The operations are consistent with ordinary packaging practices for a Python/Node.js web application server.

Minor hygiene notes: npm install with --no-audit skips vulnerability auditing, and source tracks mutable tags rather than pinned commits. These are packaging-quality concerns, not supply-chain threats, and do not affect the safety assessment.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard AUR PKGBUILD with upstream GitHub sources, checksums, and no malicious behavior detected.</summary>
